summary: This Dockerfile sets up a PHP development container with browser testing capabilities. It uses a two-stage build: first creating a builder stage that installs PHP CLI, Composer, Node.js, and Playwright dependencies, then copying those into a final PHP-FPM stage that sets up a non-root user and configures the environment for running browser-based tests with Pest PHP.

explanations.3: This special syntax comment tells Docker to use a specific version of the Dockerfile spec, enabling newer features like the cache mount syntax used later.
explanations.5: This declares a build argument with a default value; you can override it when building with --build-arg PHP_CLI_VERSION=... if you need a different PHP version.
explanations.15: The 'AS builder' part names this stage so we can reference it later; the ${PHP_CLI_VERSION} substitutes the ARG value we declared earlier.
explanations.22: These ENV variables set cache paths that will persist across all subsequent RUN commands in this stage, avoiding re-downloading the same packages.
explanations.26: The --mount directive caches the apt package cache between builds so we don't re-download packages; 'id=apt-cache' names it and 'sharing=private' keeps it isolated to this stage.
explanations.27: The 'set -eux' makes the script exit on any error, print commands before running, and show undefined variable errors—good safety practices.
explanations.32: This installs specific PHP extensions (zip and sockets support) using a Docker-provided helper script rather than manual compilation.
explanations.39: The pipe sends the downloaded installer script directly to php, which runs it with arguments specifying which Composer version to install.
explanations.42: We create a minimal package.json here just to pre-install Playwright and its dependencies during the build, saving time later.
explanations.48: Like the apt cache, this caches Composer's downloaded packages in /root/.composer between builds so reinstalls are faster.
explanations.54: We switch to the PHP-FPM base image here (not CLI) for the final stage; this creates a separate layer and we'll copy our built artifacts into it.
explanations.57: We set the timezone environment variable using the ARG we declared; this affects PHP's date functions in the container.
explanations.62: This is a fresh cache mount just for this stage's apt operations, separate from the builder stage's cache.
explanations.68: We install pcntl (process control) here which the FPM image might need but the CLI builder didn't.
explanations.77: The 'set -e -x' enables error exit and debug output for the user/group creation commands so we catch any failures.
explanations.78: We create a system group with a specific numeric ID; this ensures consistent permissions whether containers run locally or in production.
explanations.79: We create a user account with no password, add them to www-data and root groups, and assign the specific UID/GID we defined as arguments.
explanations.84: The --chown flag here changes ownership of all copied files to our non-root user so they can actually read and modify the code.
explanations.89: We add the npm binaries directory to PATH so commands like 'npx' and 'playwright' can be found without specifying the full path.
explanations.92: Switching to the non-root user means all subsequent commands and the running container will execute as this user, not root, for security.
explanations.95: This downloads Playwright's browser binaries (Chromium) into the cache path we set; now the container has actual browsers to automate for testing.
